title: Snowflake Cortex: What It Is & How To Use It In 2026
summary: Snowflake Cortex in 2026: what AI Functions, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, Cortex Agents and CoWork do, how AI Credits price them, and their limits.
body_markdown:
### Cortex AI Functions


SQL functions you run over rows:` AI_COMPLETE` for general generation,` AI_CLASSIFY` to sort text or images into your categories,` AI_FILTER` for a yes-or-no test you can put in a` WHERE` clause,` AI_AGG` to summarize a column across rows,` AI_EXTRACT` to pull fields from text, documents and images, plus` AI_SENTIMENT` ,` AI_EMBED` and` AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT` ([Snowflake: Cortex AI Functions](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql) ). They previewed in June 2025 as AISQL and became generally available on November 4, 2025 ([release note](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/other/2025-11-04-cortex-aisql-operators-ga) ). Each function has its own privilege, so admins can allow some and not others ([privileges](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-privileges-and-access) ).


### Cortex Analyst and semantic views


Cortex Analyst is Snowflake's text-to-SQL service. It answers through a semantic view, a Snowflake object that names your tables, relationships, dimensions, facts and metrics in business terms, with synonyms, custom instructions and verified queries. Semantic model YAML files on a stage still work, but Snowflake recommends semantic views for new work ([Snowflake: semantic view YAML](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/views-semantic/semantic-view-yaml-spec) ). The generated SQL runs on your warehouse and is shown with the answer. Semantic views are Snowflake's own format; definitions from dbt and other tools can move into them through Open Semantic Interchange, and our[semantic layer guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/semantic-layer) compares the options.


### Cortex Search


Cortex Search indexes text from a query you define, together with vector embeddings it computes, and serves search over it ([Snowflake: Cortex Search](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview) ). Agents use it for documents, tickets and other unstructured data.


### Cortex Agents


An agent plans the steps for a question and calls its tools: Cortex Analyst for tables, Cortex Search for text, Python code execution, a chart tool, and custom tools you write ([Snowflake: Cortex Agents](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents) ). Snowflake recommends scoping each agent narrowly before adding tools or instructions ([Snowflake: build agents](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork/build-agents) ).


### Snowflake CoWork (formerly Snowflake Intelligence)


Snowflake Intelligence became generally available on November 4, 2025 ([release note](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/other/2025-11-04-snowflake-intelligence) ) and was renamed Snowflake CoWork at Snowflake Summit in June 2026 ([Snowflake CoWork](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/snowflake-cowork/) ). It is the ready-made chat app over your agents, and queries run with each user's own credentials, so their roles and masking policies apply ([Snowflake: CoWork overview](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork) ). The old name survives in SQL, in the` CREATE SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE` privilege and the` SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE_USAGE_HISTORY` view.


### The Snowflake-managed MCP server


Generally available since November 4, 2025, it is created with` CREATE MCP SERVER` and a YAML list of tools: Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, SQL execution, an agent, or a UDF or stored procedure. Snowflake recommends exposing an agent; an Analyst tool on its own returns SQL to the client rather than running it, and it supports semantic views only ([Snowflake: managed MCP server](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp) ). The tools it exposes are the Cortex services priced below.


## Snowflake Cortex pricing


Since April 2026, most of Snowflake's AI features bill in a separate currency, AI Credits, instead of the Platform Credits that warehouses, storage and data transfer still use ([release note](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2026/other/2026-04-06-ai-services-billing-breakout) ). An AI Credit costs the same on every edition: **$2.00 with global routing** , where requests may be processed in other regions, and **$2.20 with regional routing** , where they stay in your home region or a geography you pick. Platform Credits stay priced by edition and region. Capacity discounts don't apply to AI Credits, which get their own discounts by annual contract value ([Snowflake AI pricing](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/pricing) ).
